CITY COUNCIL
MINUTES
CITY OF BALDWIN PARK
CITY COUNCIL
WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 16, 2011
7:00 p.m. COUNCIL CHAMBERS
14403 E. Pacific Avenue
Baldwin Park
Manuel Lozano, Mayor / Chair
Marlen Garcia, Mayor Pro Tem / Vice Chair Council Members / Members: Monica Garcia, Ricardo Pacheco, Susan Rubio
Maria Contreras, City Treasurer Alejandra Avila, City Clerk
The CITY COUNCIL of the City of Baldwin Park met in REGULAR SESSION at the above time and place.
CALL TO ORDER
INVOCATION
Led by Council Member Pacheco
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
ROLL CALL
Present: Council Member Monica Garcia, Council Member Pacheco, Council Member Rubio, Mayor Pro Tem Marlen Garcia, Mayor Lozano.
Absent: None.
Also Present: Chief Executive Officer Singhal, City Attorney Pannone, Recreation & Community Services Director Carrillo, Community Development Manager Castagnola, Public Works Director Galvez, Chief Hadsell, Finance Director Quijano, City Clerk Avila, City Treasurer Contreras, Deputy City Clerk Nieto.
ANNOUNCEMENTS
NONE
PROCLAMATIONS, COMMENDATIONS & PRESENTATIONS
* Certificate presentation to outgoing officers of the Baldwin Park Sister Cities Association
Mayor Lozano , joined by the Council, Clerk and Treasurer presented certificates to the outgoing officers who were in attendance at the meeting. Outgoing President Villegas shared some words about the association and some of the services they provide
* Recognition of Abran Alvarez and Veronica Menjiver for their heroic actions
Mayor Lozano , joined by the Council, Clerk and Treasurer presented a certificate to Ms. Menjiver. City Treasurer Contreras shared words about the incident and thanked them for taking care of her mother
Council Member Rubio congratulated Superior on their ground-breaking event and future grand opening
* Presentation of the Rising Star Award by ICRMA to the City of Baldwin Park
Terry Norris, Risk Manager of ICRMA provided background on the award and progress that the Human Resources division has made
* Presentation to Mayor Lozano on behalf of the L. Herreria Baseball League of Chihuahua, Mexico
Mayor Lozano was presented with a jacket from the L. Herreria Baseball League of Chihuahua, Mexico
Mayor Lozano asked that the meeting be adjourned in memory of Joseph Hummel, brother of City employee Liz Distante
PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS
Debra Asby , AQMD introduced herself as the City’s new liaison. She provided a DVD of AQMD’s state of the air that highlighted the accomplishments of 2010 and the challenges of 2011
Susan Reyes , of Senator Ed Hernandez’ office, thanked the Council for their support of the Senator and offered her services to the residents of Baldwin Park. She announced an upcoming event
Jose Luis Martinez , representing SEIU 721 thanked the City for fiscal responsibility and stated that the SEIU wanted to be partners with the City. He asked that the City work to close their current contract
Greg Tuttle , business owner complimented the opening of the Superior store, saying that it would be a good store for the community and bring in new business to the center. He also spoke about the crime that had been going on in the city
Seeing no further interest, public communications were closed at 7:26 p.m.
Council Member Pacheco announced an upcoming event for MAPS 4 College and invited the community to attend. He also reported on his attendance to the ICA Winter seminar
Continuing, Council Member Pacheco spoke about the proposed parking structure and shared the renderings with the audience
City Clerk Avila reported that the issue of the graffiti on the Metrolink right-of-way near Jones Junior High had been cleaned up and it looked much better
Addressing the comments made regarding the crime in the City, Council Member Rubio stated that there would be an item at the end of the agenda for discussion on that subject
Council Member Monica Garcia thanked City staff and partners from other agencies who were involved in the roundtable meeting to address the increase in graffiti in the City. She reported that staff and community partners were working together on the issue and were looking at jurisdictional issues that potentially hinder abatement, such as the matter with graffiti on the Metrolink right-of-way. She reported that proactive measures were being taken and noted that increases were seen in the past months. They wanted to be aware of the school holiday schedules because when the kids were not in class, there might be a higher possibility of more damage and graffiti being done. She thanked staff and partners for coming together and appreciated the communications and suppressive efforts being taken. Council Member Monica Garcia noted that a report would be provided to the Graffiti Task Force
CONSENT CALENDAR
Motion: Approve CONSENT CALENDAR
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Councilmember Marlen Garcia.

Staff Report

6. APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S DECISION TO DENY A 1) REQUEST FOR CONSIDERATION OF A MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT; 2) A CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT FOR A DENSITY BONUS OR OTHER INCENTIVES PURSUANT TO SECTION 153.531 OF THE CITY’S MUNICIPAL CODE AND STATE LAW, AND 3) A TENTATIVE TRACT MAP TO SUBDIVIDE TWO (2) LOTS INTO SEVENTEEN (17) LOTS; LOCATION: 3346-3354 VINELAND AVENUE; APPLICANT: DAVID COOK REPRESENTING DC CORPORATION; CASE NUMBERS: TM-71409 AND CP-780
Staff Report - Part 1
Staff Report - Part 2
Staff Report - Part 3
City Planner Harbin presented the report
Largest size lot 6000; smallest 3200; living space in the units are 1500 - 2200 sf; Lots 11 and 17 are approx. 1500
Council Member Pacheco asked for an explanation of the density bonus and the state law requirements. Amy Harbin, City Planner said that the law encourages developers to provide affordable housing and help the cities meet their requirements
Council Member Pacheco reported that he had gone to Stichman and spoke with the residents and said that he would not support this type of project because it was too dense. He spoke about a petition that was signed by the residents of Stichman and that he would support the residents in opposing this project
Significant would be a decrease in lot width (development incentive)
Mayor Lozano opened the public hearing for those in opposition to the project:
Craig Cook, Baldwin Park resident representing DC Corporation. He provided background on the lot and the designs
Greg Tuttle, business owner stated that his opposition was what they presented to Planning Commission, not to the amended one. Would like to see developers go into the community to get input from the residents
There were two no votes and an abstention on the vote for the PC
Mauricio Ortiz, first opposed to project but after meeting with the developer, they agree with their proposals. Wanted to see new homes with new value.
Asked for those in support:
1) Resident who lived in one of the Cooks' homes, lots of space and a big backyard. The property goes up
Brenda, Alvaro De la Torre thanked the Mayor and Council Member Monica Garcia for coming to their homes and taking into consideration what was being done. She thanked them for listening to their concerns and also thanked the developer in making the changes necessary. As long as the values continue to go up, they are in favor
Joaquin Martinez, Stichman resident spoke about the pride that he and his neighbors have in their community. He said he was opposed to the first proposed plan but was in support of the newly proposed project
Marie Contreras, resident spoke in favor of the project and the Cook's and that her parents purchased a home when they were relocated
Cruz Baca, resident said that it was time to celebrate because the Cook family took the time, as well as the Mayor & Monica, to speak to the people and listen to them and translate into something that they wanted. They need to listen more, there is a voice in the community, there are many good things in the City and they wanted to be heard and respected
Frank Maroni, plumbing company had worked with the Cook's and said that they are very good businessmen and had completed 28 projects with them. The project was very important to them and would make a difference of their businesses' survival. Encouraged the approval of the project
Abel, West Covina resident, Superior Construction had been doing work with the Cook's for several years and said that they needed the work and encouraged the Council to support the project
Russ Simonsen, Superior Construction pointed out that in the past he would not have to come to a Council meeting or work on a small project, but said that it was important for him to be there to ask for support. This amount of work impacts his income
Seeing no further interest, the public hearing was closed
Council Member Rubio thanked the residents for organizing themselves and thanked the Cook's for meeting with the residents
Council Member Pacheco stated that he had been opposed to the 17 unit roject but if the developer was willing to look at a smaller project, he would be willing to give the deveoper a chance to present a different project that would be aligned with what the community wanted
Mayor Pro Tem Marlen Garcia clarified for the audience that the City has designated areas for projects, if the rules are followed, then they can be built and designed, etc. She explained the approval process via the Planning Commission. She said that the Commission did not support it and she thanked them for their work.
She said that she was glad that it did come before the Council and felt that they should come to the Council for review. She said that she did not have the opportunity to see the PC report. When she saw what was proposed, she was not in favor of it. She suggested a process where a neighborhood or community outreach should be done, as their input is needed. She said this was a good example of the community coming together to get something done
The residents do care about the projects. She said that she has supported the Cooks' in the past and that she was hard on them because she wanted them to have affordable units. She loved to see when the residents could afford the homes. She wanted to make sure that there were quality projects in the city. They need to start looking at a process where the oness is on the developer to reach out to the community
Developers are held to high standards and the Council needed to look at a process to make sure all these needs are met. Did not want it to get to the point where a developer spent lots of money but then the community doesn't want it.
Council Member Monica Garcia thanked the residents for being part of this process and it's important for their input to be heard. There is a lot to gain in the process and that undeveloped lots will eventually be developed. She said that she opposed the 17 unit project because she believed that neighborhoods needed to be protected. There needed to be cohesiveness with the developments that came in. She believed in higher density where it made sense, for example on BP Blvd. Similar types of housing. Thanked the Cook's for reaching out to the residents and agreed that moving forward, they involve the residents.
She was glad that the community chimed in, she opposed the 17 unit project and consider the 15 unit
Mayor Lozano thanked the residents and recommended that the 17 unit be denied (ML/MONICA)
Motion: Approve Uphold the Planning Commission decision to deny the project and waive further reading, read by title only and adopt Resolution No. 2011-007 entitled, "A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BALDWIN PARK UPHOLDING THE PLANNING COMMISSION'S DENIAL OF 1) A CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT FOR DENSITY BONUS OR OTHER INCENTIVES IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 153.531 OF THE CITY'S MUNICIPAL CODE AND STATE LAW; AND 2) A TENTATIVE TRACT MAP TO SUBDIVIDE TWO (2) LOTS INTO SEVENTEEN (17) LOTS FOR RESIDENTIAL PURPOSES; LOCATION: 3346-3354 VINELAND AVENUE; APPLICANT: DAVID COOK, REPRESENTING DC CORPORATION; CASE NUMBERS: CP-780 AND TM-71409"
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Councilmember Monica Garcia.
Vote: Motion carried 5-0.
Ayes: Councilmember Marlen Garcia; Mayor Lozano; Councilmember Monica Garcia; Councilmember Rubio; Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco
Ricardo asked that it be stated for the record that he was not in support of the 17
Council Member Pacheco suggested bringing back the project and propose the 15 units
City Attorney Pannone said that applicant would go thru the process with Planning Division.
Craig Cook stated that he had asked for the item to be continued
City Attorney Pannone said that the Council had the authority to take it from the PC
Council Member Pacheco asked if it could be brought to the Council directly and City Attorney Pannone said that it would have to go thu PC. The Council had the authority to bring it back to them. He said they'd conditionally approve the appeal to what has been proposed
City Attorney Pannone suggested a process
Amy Harbin, City Planner talked about the state mandated deadlines and the limitations they would have with regards to the project.
Council Member Monica Garcia asked Amy Harbin, City Planner if they continue the item and send it back to staff; would the CEQA process still take 21 days? yes since there are significant changes and recirculation.
Council Member Rubio asked if staff time would be saved by continuing vs.
City Attorney Pannone said that if it went to PC, it would still have to come back to the Council
Council Member Pacheco asked if they could consider rescinding the reso. City Attorney Pannone said that the project had to be more defined but it would not be able to come back in a month
Council Member Monica Garcia asked how long it would take to brign the item back before Council. Amy said first meeting April meeting, best case scenario. Amy said that it was a high priority issue to the developer; the Council could remand it back to the pc and it could come back to the Coundcil as an advisory item
Amy said that they would start over and if the PC approves it, it would stop there. She could bring it to the Council as an advisory item.
Council Member Rubio wanted to see the final project come back to the Council. joe suggested rescinding the action, continue the appeal to a date uncertain, direct staff and developer to treat the item as an item that would have come to the PC instead of the Council.
Motion: Rescind the original motion and (see Joe's comments on the further action)
Moved by Councilmember Rubio, seconded by Councilmember Marlen Garcia.
Vote: Motion carried 5-0.
Ayes: Councilmember Marlen Garcia; Mayor Lozano; Councilmember Monica Garcia; Councilmember Rubio; Mayor Pro Tem Pacheco
Council Member Pacheco wanted to see a letter from the Council be sent to the residents explaining what was taking place
Mayor Pro Tem Marlen Garcia said it should be sent to everyone on the list (radius)
Motion: Approve Matter continued to date uncertain, be processed as a PC
Moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Councilmember Marlen Garcia.

Mayor Lozano opened the public hearing for those in opposition to the moratorium:
1) Cruz Baca said that the healthy choices needed to start w/ parents
mathew galindo resident of bp
existing drive thru would not be removed just clarifying.
Peter Winningham
revisons regards to the existing restaurants
not sure what they mean. He spoke about the report and criteria, etc
